utterances.text: He wasn't there with us. He had stripped us earlier in Jusuf Memic's house and mistreated us and abused us, but he wasn't over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that your son testified that he was immediately outside the window, would he be mistaken?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I objection to that question. Clearly's he entitled to make that submission to the Chamber in evaluating her credibility, but is it really for this witness to judge the credibility of her own son? It seems a perfectly appropriate question to ask her whether she saw Milan Susnjar but it seems inappropriate to ask her to give an opinion with respect to her own son's testimony. That's for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But he could ask her whether she could be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe the appropriate question would be is it possible she's mistaken, but to confront her with the evidence of her son again I submit that's argument for the final submissions, and the Chamber will have to consider contradictions between the evidence and make its own evaluation of the individual witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe he can ask you whether she can be mistaken. Put it to her that way, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it possible that you're mistaken about Milan Susnjar being there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us who were in that group, nobody can say exactly the same thing, because they haven't seen all of them, the same things. One saw one part, another saw another part. Milan Susnjar was there. Back in that other house he stripped us naked. In this other place I -- I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you testified that you jumped out the window immediately or very quickly after your son. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three minutes after my son, because I couldn't jump straight after him because of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But regardless, the windows provided the only exit to this room. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The windows were the only exit for those who were able to take it, but this window next to the first one, I couldn't reach it because there were other people crowded there. And when this man turned away the rifle from this window, I jump out of it landing straight in front of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the person with the flashlight, was the flashlight pointed right at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was shining the light on the windows. I don't know whether he was shining it straight at me. Maybe he didn't shine it at me directly, because if he had, maybe they would have killed me there and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When someone is using a flashlight and you're looking at that person, isn't it true that it tends to make the area behind the flashlight very dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that Mitar Vasiljevic wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it possible that you're mistaken that Mitar Vasiljevic was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you're not mistaken because you've known Mitar Vasiljevic for a very long time and knew him on site. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know him as a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You knew him as a citizen of Visegrad, a Serbian, who served Muslims and socialised with Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly we all socialised regardless: Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic, Djuro Petar; we didn't pay attention to the origin of names. We all lived fine up until the war. How the communities began to hate each other after the war I can't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But other than your involvement in this, when did you start to hear stories about Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing to hear. Mr. Milan Lukic came to the door. All these other people who had perished in the fire knew him, as well as Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Susnjar, nicknamed "Lalco." They all knew them. I see you sir, now, here in the courtroom. Five years later, wherever we meet, I will recognise you. I will tell you, "Good afternoon, sir, you are so-and-so." I still have a good memory as far as I'm able to see although I'm a peasant with only four years of school. I have lived through all of this, and I still have some schooling. Even if I didn't, I know what I know. You cannot convince me that all of what I'm saying is not true and that I had not lived through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, that's not what I asked you. I asked you when did you hear other stories about Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic amongst either the Muslims before or after this ordeal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the people who occupied other positions knew that Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic had been killing people around the villages. They were mistreating people, abusing them, taking girls to be raped before we were taken -- before we were chased out to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it must have hurt you to know these citizens were having these stories told about them, including such violence against your people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly the people were seized by panic and fear. They went to hide in the woods, leaving their homes. Everything was destroyed. There's not a single house standing. There's no one -- nothing to come back to. Houses will be rebuilt, but the people will not come back, at least not those who lost their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would -- would it be fair that if you were able to hold them responsible here for that incident, that is like holding them responsible for the other things that you had heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't come here to accuse anyone. I came only to tell what I have lived through. The court is here to decide and to decide what is right and what is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we have P59 back, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, looking at this picture again, isn't it true that we can't see the window that you escaped from because it is off to the left and obstructed by the edge of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But that second window is only about two metres from the one that we can see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was two metres or there were two windows immediately side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you described this room as -- as -- and I was guesstimating from your estimate that this was about a three-by-four metre room.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't measure them. I just said roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, to put 70 people in this room it would be very, very crowded. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's why I stepped on people's feet to get to the window to get some fresh air, because I realised immediately either they will burn us to death or take us out to slit our throats. Those who still remembered the war, unlike me, realised immediately what would happen, and they kept telling us, "You, young people who can, run for it." I pushed my way together with my child to the window, and as the explosion happened, Mitar Vasiljevic and Lukic were at the corner of house and two people jumped out before me. I pushed my child out, and I followed as soon as I can barefoot. I had lost my shoes in pushing through the crowd, so I jumped out barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, I don't want to interrupt you because I know you're speaking but that wasn't necessarily the question that I'd ask you, and so I'd ask you please so that this doesn't take too long and inconvenience you too long that you answer my questions as I ask them. Can we do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, as you had to push your way through people, how many people did you have to push your way through to get to the window? You said you stepped on feet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you cram 70 people in that room, you have to push through how many people? Through all those who were in front of me. Now when you get into a small room you have to push your way through to get to the window, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am, you do. So when you're at the window all the people you had to push through now block your sight between yourself and the front door. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not necessarily. It doesn't block the sight. They saw me well, too, and they are telling me, "Why are you pushing," and I said I wanted to take some fresh air. It wasn't really very dark. There was lighting outside and there was lighting from the houses nearby. There was not a lot, but it was enough to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: There was no light source inside the room; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no light bulb inside. Nobody turned on the light, because nobody thought of lighting the light bulb. They were too afraid to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so the only light source would be ambient light from homes across the ravine or whatever could come through the front door into a darkened basement. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the windows, not the door, because these windows were facing the lights, and the entrance is on the other wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there were several people between -- once you were able to get yourself next to the window, this was before the fire started; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the fire started, I was already by the window with my son. When the fire started, two witnesses that I named earlier jumped out, because that lady shattered the windowpane.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question I asked you though is all the people that you pushed through are now blocking your view to the door. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all we expected from that door was someone to come in and kill us. We were only looking at the windows to see if we could jump out. If we dare jump out, because if we don't take the risk, we'll burn alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But the people between you and the door blocked your view of the door. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't even looking at the door. I was focusing on the window in order to save my life and my child's life.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true you could not see the face of the person who open the door and put something inside to catch it on fire because it was impossible, because you were looking at the window, that there was not enough light come in and all the people that you had pushed through were now in between you and blocking your view of the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people were all sitting down, sir. Those were elderly people, infirmed people, children. They had all sat down. Some women, I hope the Court will excuse me, had to breast feed, give some bread to the children, and the door opened when Mr. Milan brought the device. Everybody saw him. I was not the only one who saw him. Everybody saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Mr. Kurspahic, before he passed away, said that the door blew open as if --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour. I have the same objection. I mean, the appropriate question would be isn't it a fact that the door blew open or something the same factual assertion, but to start putting witnesses up against each other and -- I think is an inappropriate way of posing the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think she may have indicated that she spoke with the witness afterwards, but I may be mistaken as to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Spoken with Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The older Kurspahic, the father, passed away in 1996, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Kurspahic that she spoke to was the Kurspahic that testified here a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question was if -- if there was testimony regarding the elderly Kurspahic, that he was blown in and the door was blown open as if by a rocket, could she be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could you be mistaken? Could the door have been blown open by a rocket, as if by a rocket, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What rocket are you talking about? Come on. Come off it. Nobody would have survived, although I don't know much about ammunition. Rockets down planes. The whole house would have been destroyed with us in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, I was merely referring to what information another survivor indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She has answered. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you did speak that you -- you did indicate that you spoke to his son, Huso Kurspahic, afterwards; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did see each other later, but I wouldn't say we had much of a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You know that he was a police commander for the Muslims at that point. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He worked on the police force. Not only he but some Serbs did as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I just want to know about your knowledge of Huso.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a neighbour. Our houses were very close together. We all lived as one community, so I know where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And as the duty of a police officer when he spoke to you as a survivor, did he take a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took some notes briefly because I wouldn't tell him the first time what had actually happened to his sisters and his parents. He took some notes, but I wasn't looking at him. He did ask me after his family, but I wouldn't tell him then that they had all died.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did he ever reduce a statement to writing so that you could review it and sign it about the crimes of that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign anything for him. Whether he wrote some more I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now let's talk about describing the perpetrators. What was Mitar Vasiljevic wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A black hat and a black suit when he came to Jusuf Memic's house. And when he came to that house he would come barefoot. That's by day. And he also had a black raincoat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so this is how you remember him during the day when he handed Mr. Memic the note that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I remember him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that note was purported to preserve your safety?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just so the record is correct, I believe the evidence is the note was handed to Mr. Mujo Halilovic and not Mr. Memic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But the note though was for the safety of the occupants of the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic came and said that we should put up there until the morning when we would be taken to Kladanj. He took out a small flask and offered Mr. Halilovic a shot of brandy, and he also handed a piece of paper saying, "Don't worry, you'll be safe."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How was Mitar dressed at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night he was again wearing a black suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Still barefoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see whether he was barefoot that night, but he was barefoot when he came that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Still black cowboy hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how was the person you believed to be Milan Lukic, how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Green-brown camouflage military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how about the other Milan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other Milan, Susnjar, nicknamed "Lalco" was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what about Sredoje?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We already received the answer that witness did not see by her eyes Sredoje Lukic, during the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you see Sredoje, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sredoje was around the house, and Edhem Kurspahic saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You did not see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not. There was Bosko Djuric, Sredoje Lukic, Milan Susnjar, Mitar Vasiljevic. In fact, I'm sorry, Milan Lukic and Milan Susnjar. And there were others whom I couldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you don't know what Sredoje was wearing at any time during the day is what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We already have a clear answer on this question, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When I agreed she indicated she didn't see him at night, but I think she indicated she saw him earlier in the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's a different time. Let the witness answer a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So is it true you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as soon as other people saw him it means they did not make it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember everything that I stated as I stated it. What I'm saying is that if the other people saw him, they were not lying because they knew very well who is a next door neighbour, who is from Uzice, who is from where.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was Bosko wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothes. He worked as a taxi driver in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You said there were other people present. How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were in civilian clothes. Some were in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many total people there that weren't of the victims of this tragedy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Give me a range, please. I won't ask you to be specific.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five, six.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Including the five that you've named, or five or six in addition to the five you've named?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So there's a total of 10 to 12 people there during this time is what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where were the other people located, generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If there were only two ways out of the house, through the windows and through the doors, why would they need to be on the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that people wouldn't escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that I saw, they were armed. I suppose the others were, too, because nobody went around without a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that you'd never seen Milan Lukic before that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that day I did used to see him around the town, sometimes on a bus, although he worked in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him before June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date, but I used to see him when we were sitting in a hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new hotel called Panos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you see him at the new hotel at Panos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, but I would see him when I would come from the field. Our group would stop by to have a drink and dress. Mitar was a waiter. It's his colleague and a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you knew this how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How did we know? Well, Visegrad is not New York. You know your neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many years before the war, if it was that long, did you see Milan at the Panos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him too often before the war because I was working in the field, but we did run into each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: As specific as you can. I'm not asking for a date, but it would be nice if we could get a month and a year or a season and a year. Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date or the month or the year, because I didn't make a mental note of when I met someone knowing that I would one day come here to tell you when and where I met these people, but we did meet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And how many times did you see him at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within two or three months when we would go to the restaurant. It wasn't a habit of ours to go to restaurants frequently, so that is when I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So do I understand, then, that you saw him at the hotel over a period of three months, at the restaurant? Do you have any recollection of how many times you actually saw him at the hotel or the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once in three or four months. We would either meet in town on Wednesdays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was talking about the hotel. You told us that you saw Milan at the hotel, and I was trying to find out from you was it once? Was it one time you saw him at the hotel or twice or three times? Just how many.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, twice a year we would see each other in passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was that at the hotel or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you remember what year that was? It may be difficult, but do you have any -- any idea as to when that was? Or if you don't remember the exact year, how many years before 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot remember exactly either the year or the date. I wasn't thinking about it. You just meet a person, pass by them, say hello. So I cannot remember the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To follow up on the Judge's question, ma'am, was there a formal introduction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I knew Milan from before, so there was no need for anyone to introduce him by saying, "This is our neighbour Milan Lukic," or Mitar Vasiljevic, or someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I just want to focus on how you knew Milan Lukic before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Koritnik for 20 years. My children went to school there. We attended dances. I know the whole county and all the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet isn't it true that the village that Milan comes from is over 20 kilometres away by car or driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe from the town, but from the village of Koritnik it's not such a distance to the village of Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you had business over in Rujiste all the time so you knew his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Klasnik, I had a close relative whom I went to visit, and on my way there I passed through Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so how old was Milan when you first saw him, when you passed through Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't estimate his age. He was a young boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How young?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How young. He was young. I wasn't at his birth to know how old he was. He was around 20, maybe a little bit over 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So the last time you saw him was 20, or the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As he was growing up, a boy. He was 20. Of course he's older now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So are you saying the first time you ever saw Milan Lukic, he was 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was 20, but he was -- I wasn't able to judge his age.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this is some knowledge you gained passing through Rujiste on your way to Klasnik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't knowledge. She said she saw him passing through Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I guess the question would be, ma'am, how do you know it's Milan Lukic, seeing a 20-year-old man in Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody knew where everybody lives. We went to school together. We attended parent-teacher meetings together, so you knew who everybody's son was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have a son that was 20 the same time that Milan was 20, or were you 20 at the same time Milan was 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an elderly son who used to go to Prelovo to attend dances when he was 11, and he married three times in -- during his 30 years of life.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how does that give you personal knowledge of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific personal knowledge about Milan Lukic. He was a neighbour who was growing up in our proximity, and I cannot say anything else that does not stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you don't have to pass through Rujiste to go from Koritnik to Klasnik? Koritnik, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could take another route as well, but one would go through Rujiste as well. The village of Omeragici and Sitarevo and Kamenica behind Klasnik and Rujiste are the farthest villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't that a way out of the way to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the village of Sitarevo but not to Rujiste. One could easily walk there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you saw this 20-year-old Milan Lukic, who pointed him out to you? Did you stop? Did you speak to his family, something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk to him, and nobody pointed him to me, and of course I knew how everyone was called. Another witness will appear here who was in the same classroom with him. Her name is Latifa. She was married to Omer Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many of the witnesses have you spoken to since the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't talked to anyone specifically about things. Everyone went through horrible times. Latifa lost her husband, her father, and her 11-year-old son, and she is currently living in Austria.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old is Latifa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know her age, but she was married when she was 21 or 22. She had two daughters and the son Aner who died along with his father in Kremna. When her father-in-law, Hasan Kurspahic, and his wife Meha came to her to Sarajevo she said, "I want to see them," and they used to say that Mr. Milan Lukic took out Aner Kurspahic and Fikret who was with the army, I don't know, in Belgrade. They took out her son Aner who was left behind in Kremna, and Latifa asked this gentleman to let her husband and her brother-in-law go, and I asked her, "How did you forget about your son?" And she said, "I don't know." And they still don't know anything about these two men and this child, and if necessary she will come here to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you've had a lot of talking with other witnesses in this case. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For the record, this person is not a witness in this case so there's no confusion about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have no evidence that this person is a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You had indicated, though, that you had these conversations with Latifa well after your surviving this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you had no information about Latifa's knowledge of Milan Lukic before the incident at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed in our homes for another day or two. Fikret, Hasan Kurspahic's son, was working in Belgrade in the military service, and he came there to take his father and mother to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When was this? When was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before we set off -- or, rather, before we were expelled from our homes we found out that they did not manage to pass through, that there was another soldier who put Hasan Kurspahic, Meja Kurspahic, and Latifa and two little girls, one was 40 days old, and put them in a car and they managed to pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you had gathered just simply information about Milan Lukic before, but you really didn't know him and you couldn't have described him. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I did not gather any information. This man told us about those two sons who were never found. I cannot give you all the details here. It really upsets me. I'm not made of steel. I went through all this. Just by looking at this picture you will know how I feel, sir, if you have any sympathy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you really didn't know him and couldn't have described him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milan Lukic, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milan Lukic was thinner. He wasn't as sturdy as he is now. He was a very --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At 20 years old, what was his hair like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as it is now, brownish, unless he dyes his hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What his haircut, the cut of his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also short.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Always short?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] so if he had regular haircut it was short. If not, it was a bit long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have been with this witness now for about an hour and perhaps 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Has it been that long?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I haven't heard from the time keeper. One hour and 20 minutes. One hour and 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And how much time am I allotted, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe the Prosecution had quite a bit of time. Is it standard that we get 60 per cent of the Prosecution's time or which is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's a matter in which I exercise a judgement. How much more time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm kind of working my way backwards and I'm going to go through some of the statements including the one that was introduced, so I'm kind of working my way back so you can see where we're at, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, give me an idea of how much more time you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Less than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I would like to take you back to the village, actually -- or actually, no. Excuse me. Tell me about Dragomir Gavrilovic. Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragomir Gavrilovic was a young man. He used to come to our village before we were dislocated. He maltreated people. He threatened to kill us, but not in our village so that we wouldn't exude stench.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you say that again, ma'am? He didn't want to kill you in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know him to be a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that he was a member of the SDS. I didn't pay attention to that. I wasn't interested. Whether he joined some party after the war, I also don't know that, but as a child, he used to live in Dalmatia with his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet you included him in the statement as the neighbours who attacked your village. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did he appear to have a position of authority as that attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he had as long as he dare to come and maltreat elderly people in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did it appear that other people followed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what transpired among them. He threatened us. He at one point caught my child, VG-38, and he said he would cut his throat with his teeth, not with his knife. He was chasing him behind our houses, cursed his mother, insulted him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was this -- when was this, the day, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 13th of June, one day before we set off on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say that the evacuation and extermination of your village began with your neighbours who you could name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I named my neighbours on numerous occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And they orchestrated this evacuation and deportation from your village. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it appeared to be organised by your neighbours. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did organise that. However, who gave them orders I don't know. The orders must have come from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could it have simply come from Dragomir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't ask him. He knows who he gave orders to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that the first time that you gave a -- or enter the square of Visegrad next to the Red Cross you were met by regular police officers, and you named them. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were policemen, and some men in camouflage uniforms. I was afraid to look at them. And I believe that if you had been in the same situation, sir, you also would be afraid to look at anyone. You would just keep your eyes on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true, ma'am, that Drago Gavrilovic was also a member of the Crisis Staff in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know? I did not meet with Drago to ask him if he was a member of a station or a staff or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You only knew him as a man that abused you and your village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Unnecessary. Next question, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that you indicated, though, in one of your statements that Drago was a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I never said anything of the kind in any of my statements. He's a neighbour of ours. His house is not far from our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true though that his parents had a home in -- in the Glavica neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His parents are divorced. His mother hails from Dalmatia. She was married to Stevo Gavrilovic, who is deceased. I don't remember exactly when, perhaps a year ago. He grew up with his mother in Dalmatia, and when the war broke out, he came to live with his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did his father have a home in Pionirska in Glavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And please tell me about Ilija Gavrilovic. Isn't it true that he was a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not before the war. He is a police officer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you wouldn't know whether he was before the war or at least at the time of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war he joined the police. He wasn't a policeman before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true through that when you were brought to Visegrad you were brought to the police station right next to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but the Red Cross was not by the police station. It was in the Jondza Street closer to the new hotel on the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that your escorts, including Mr. Grujic, went into the police station as you continued on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did go to the police station, whereas we continued on our way to the Red Cross building, which wasn't open. It was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you indicated in your statement that Dusan Grujic is a tall blonde?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The man is dead. I have nothing to say about a dead man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution -- this witness has given several statements. The Prosecution would certainly appreciate just a reference so that we may following along.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's the 1998 statement of 12th and 13th of February. I believe the Prosecution may have referred to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Dusan Grujic -- well, let me just ask you. Did he have tattoos on his arms of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did have a tattoo. I don't remember the picture. Something he had made in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that as you entered the town you were approached by several police, Serb police, that started harassing you and swearing at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those slurs were outside the new hotel when we hid under a poplar tree from the rainfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that some of the police started suggesting that your group be killed and thrown into the river as you waited at the Red Cross building for about an hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly there was all sort of abuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that finally actually a police officer is the one that told you to go to the Mahala neighbourhood to wait and that you could stay in those houses till the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you simply didn't know the name of this Serbian police officer. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't even look at him carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that they had insignias on their uniform that were different from before the war. Can you remember them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had some insignia looking like flags, blue. There was a little flag both on the caps and on the sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were there the Serbian insignias of the White Eagles on those caps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no White Eagles, just a little flag, a narrow patch on the sleeve and on a cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you didn't see any White Eagles that afternoon or evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't looking whether it was white or black.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you didn't see any Eagles that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, but I heard from other people that some troops of that sort had been present as well, but I personally didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say that at the time that you started walking to the Mahala neighbourhood, the only ones that knew you were going there were the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Nobody told me whether they knew we were going to the Nova Mahala or whether the police was aware or the civilian population was aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where is this taking us, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Alternative theories of the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's simply alternative theories of the Defence. Alternative perpetrators and knowledge in terms of the situation with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, tell me more specifically, because I need to know your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're suggesting what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm suggesting that the formal police of Visegrad, including members of which are some of the family members that took them from their village, which included Mr. Ilija Gavrilovic, had more knowledge in terms of the circumstances of their -- of their deportation as well as ultimately what was going to happen to them. Also, Your Honour, considering the fact that it was a police officer that told them where to go does sort of form the basis of some of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You must move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I will, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't consider that to be very relevant, so just move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true, though, you gave a statement in this case actually all the way back to the 14th of August, 1995? And this was a statement to the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zenica. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1995. I gave so many statements, I couldn't count them; and I'm not sure to whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in your original statement you didn't know the names of the two Chetniks who told you to go to Visegrad? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who told us to go to Visegrad and then continue by bus to Kladanj, it was Micun, Lipovac. Micun was the nickname of the person named Milorad. And Dusan Grujic, who is late, Dusan Grujic. They said it was ethnic cleansing. Now, two other persons stopped us outside Greben village, and I don't know who these two were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Ilija Gavrilovic followed you from Greben to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Milorad Lipovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you arrived according to your first statement that we have, when you arrive in Visegrad the -- one the Serbian police officer you actually did recognise, Brane Tesovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And also his brother Boro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at that point in time in your first statement you said that there was 150 men, women, and children that were being forced onto the bridge and their throats slit right in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not that many, but there were quite a lot of them, and many bodies flowed down the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And a bearded Chetnik about 50 was cutting throats and throwing them off the Drina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you made no reference to this slaughter in any of your subsequent statements. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are many things I didn't mention because I can't -- I can't force myself to remember it all. Even this is upsetting me enough. I'm not made of wood, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You indicated -- but it was quite a scene, because you indicated that people were crying. Mothers begged them to spare their children, and the screams were terrible, but the Chetniks cut people's throats shouting, "Cut the balijas," a derogatory term, "Cut their throats. Hit them between the legs. Cut off his" -- he won't be needing it any more and so on. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened in Jusuf Memic's house. A man was kicked in the crotch to make him spread his legs so he can be abused, but on that bridge there were just screams and cries and begging to spare them. There are other witnesses who can tell you how the bridge was washed from all the blood with a water tank. It was hosed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In your first statement you indicated that your co-worker, Brane Tesovic, a police officer forced people to come to be slaughters, but you did not see him cut anyone's throat on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't cut those. Another man did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you heard from Amira Savanija, another co-worker that Brane and his brother Boro had taken away her husband and cut their throats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Her husband, her father-in-law, and her son-in-law. It was in Unista just above the dam where the hydro power plant was being built.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet for this court earlier in your testimony you forgot the slaughter on the bridge even though this should have been in your mind as you entered Visegrad, after coming from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not clear to me what you mean by that, yet for this court earlier in your testimony you forgot this slaughter. What are you saying exactly, that she didn't testify to this in examination-in-chief or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Or in any of her subsequent statements. I mean, this is -- to me, maybe I'm being naive, but I think if my village was being brought to the town of Visegrad and on the bridge they're cutting throats and throwing them off the bridge, in her first statement and only statement she said 150 people had gathered and the screams and the cries of mothers begging for their children, that would be something that would come out in the forefront of the memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, as far as the examination-in-chief is concerned, she -- she answered questions. She -- her testimony's in response to questions asked. However, Witness, what counsel is saying, that in none of your subsequent statements did you mention anything about these awful happenings on the bridge, the cutting of throats and throwing people off the bridge. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot tell the whole story from the beginning. I would go crazy. I made it as short as I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- making outlines in my statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please move on, Mr. Alarid. Another Judge -- my colleague says another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I would ask is that the English version, which has been uploaded as 1D10-0155 be introduced under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is admitted as Exhibit 1D29 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Let me just check my notes, Your Honour, and I will probably pass the witness. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My name is Djuro Cepic, and I appear here for the Defence of Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nice to meet you. I'm VG-13.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Before I start examining you, let me say I quite understand and sympathise with your suffering, your suffering and that of your son.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, but I hardly think you can understand it if you haven't experienced it yourself. It's very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I understand you quite well. People carry the consequences for a long time afterwards, even for smaller things let alone something like this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'll try to be as clear as I can in my questions, and I would appreciate brief answers, if possible. Madam, I maintain to you that Mr. Sredoje Lukic was not involved in the incident in Pionirska Street that day. He was very far from Visegrad. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand you're asking the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Sredoje Lukic surrendered voluntarily to this court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that's entirely accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the question of whether surrender is voluntary is quite often a difficult matter to determine. Let's move on. I'm not sure that much turns on it, so let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you tell me, madam, this other son you have who had several marriages, what year was he born in?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You were 19 when he was born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The other son was born in 1978?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you used to see Sredoje Lukic and Huso Kurspahic on patrol. Did you also see them after your children were born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I meant the period between '75 and '78, actually, for the record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me about this terrible incident. I have to underline "terrible." As a mother, did you always keep your son by your side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So throughout the incident he was by your side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yesterday and today I listened carefully to your responses given to Mr. Groome and the president of the Chamber, and you said clearly that you had not seen Sredoje Lukic that day in Pionirska Street. Instead, you heard about his presence there from Edhem.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You cannot tell us, I suppose, whether the two of them knew each other, Edhem and Sredoje, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since Edhem recognised him, he must have known him, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Translation is in line 24, "must have know him," but the witness said [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: That is rendered by the words "I suppose."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you really say he probably knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He certainly knew him, because he passed by on patrol more than once.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You don't remember which was Edhem's location in the house? Was he close to the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look where everyone was standing. We were all in one room.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Similarly in the evening when you were moving from Memic's house to the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We filed one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But Edhem was behind you, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: After the incident you were first given some medical assistance by Mrs. Bakira Cecic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, this is an identification sheet. I will just mention the codes and designations, not names, because we are in open session. When you crossed over to the Muslim side, did VG-122 give you any medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I moved from Kosovo Polje to the left bank of the Drina, I got some medical assistance at the Red Cross. That woman sent me to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... please. 2D732. Statement of VG-122.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is only one mistake in this statement. Otherwise, everything you said is correct. You highly appreciate this person as a very credible one. I'm talking about VG-122?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I went to see him at Crni Vrh. He bandaged me and then he sent me off to the hospital in Gorazde. I was full of maggots and I was in a very poor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm looking at my screen and I see the statement of another witness. Is counsel proposing to show the statement of another witness to this particular witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is all from the Prosecution's list and this is a list that we received from them and in this list this medical aid is mentioned, and I would like the witness to clarify certain things for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then it would seem to me, Your Honour, then to put questions about the medical aid. I'm not sure what benefit there is to showing the witness a very suggestive thing such as a statement from another witness. In fact the rules of this Tribunal require us to segregate witnesses before they come and for the very reason that this only confuses the fact-finding process. I believe he can put the -- whatever assertion he believes is in this statement to the witness, but he can do that without having the witness read another witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is some merit in that, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, we already heard from you that VG-122 examined you and gave you medical help.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you explain to him what had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me where I came from, from what hell had I emerged. He gave me medical assistance that evening. In the evening I crossed through the woods and went to a hospital in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understood. I understood the last instruction. Just for the record, because this witness VG-122 mentioned different last name of the witness, and that was the purpose of this, just to confirm that the witness was there and medical help is given by the VG-122, and that VG-122 received the informations about this incident. Thank you. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, my learned colleague Groome asked you as well about the statement of the 5th of May, 2008, that you gave to the county prosecutor in Sarajevo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you gave that to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... system the number 2D670.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, is this your signature here at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll down B/C/S version, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is also your signature; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And here again that's your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... document my learned friend Mr. Groome already requested to be marked for identification. I would like kindly to request admission of this document because I don't see any -- any problem to be admitted now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would just ask that it remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: P62, does that assist the registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, in the meantime, in late 1992, did you give an interview to the Sarajevo television about this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That was in late 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to now -- now draw a line that approximates the flow of that creek in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It runs all the way from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. And could I ask you to put in X to indicate approximately where you were shortly after you jumped out of the burning building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was here under the elder bush.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that with an X, please. Okay. I think you have done that. Just to make it clearer, could I ask you to circle that X? Maybe it will make it a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that as Exhibit -- I tender 65 ter number 175.5 with the markings of VG-13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted as Exhibit P63 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In cross-examination, you said, "Edhem shouted that we were followed by Sredoje Lukic." Could I ask you, this Edhem that you were referring to, where did he live, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, would he have had the same opportunities to see Sredoje Lukic patrolling that village as you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly, since he knew him from before. He was an elderly man. He knew the whole surrounding of Visegrad, not just one village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, VG-13. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: VG-13, you are a person of admirable courage. You have given your evidence. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of September, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.
